extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (authors) and peer reviewers preparing or assessing Registered Reports for Scientific Reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing, submitting, and reviewing Registered Reports at the journal Scientific Reports, covering Stage 1 (protocol review) and Stage 2 (full study review) requirements, data sharing, and deviations/withdrawals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage peer review and Registered Report format
rubrics_metrics.description: A Registered Report is an original research article which undergoes a two-stage peer review process: Stage 1 (methods and proposed analyses peer-reviewed prior to data collection) and Stage 2 (final manuscript with results and discussion re-reviewed). Protocols meeting stringent methodological rigour are provisionally accepted (AIP) and pre-registered before data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final acceptance does not depend on the results obtained, but only on the rigour of the methodology and how well developed the research question is. The format is designed to minimise publication and research bias and allows separate reporting of exploratory (unregistered) analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 required contents (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial submissions must include a description of the key research question and background literature, hypotheses (where applicable), experimental procedures, analysis pipeline, a sampling plan (statistical power analysis or Bayesian equivalent), and pilot data (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use the provided Stage 1 template to prepare submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 cover letter: scientific case
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letter must include a brief scientific case for consideration; the journal aims to publish original research of outstanding methodological rigour and welcomes scientifically justified replication studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 cover letter: support and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letter must state that all necessary support (e.g. funding, facilities) and approvals (e.g. ethics) are in place for the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts will generally be considered only for studies that can commence immediately; authors with alternative plans should contact the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 cover letter: anticipated timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letter must provide an anticipated timeline for completing the study if the initial submission is accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 cover letter: data/materials/code sharing commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letter must include a statement confirming that the authors agree to share their raw data, any digital study materials, computer code (if relevant), and laboratory log for all published results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 cover letter: protocol registration commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letter must confirm that, following Stage 1 acceptance in principle, the authors agree to register their approved protocol on a recognized repository, either publicly or under private embargo until Stage 2 manuscript submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 cover letter: withdrawn registration agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letter must state that if the authors later withdraw their paper, they agree to the Journal publishing a short summary of the pre-registered study as a Withdrawn Registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction requirements at Stage 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction should include a review of relevant literature that motivates the research question and a full description of the experimental aims and hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After AIP, the Introduction cannot be altered except to correct factual or typographic errors and to change tense from future to past.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: sample characteristics and inclusion/exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods must include a full description of proposed sample characteristics, including criteria for data inclusion and exclusion (e.g., outlier extraction). Procedures for objectively defining exclusion criteria due to technical errors or other reasons must be specified, including how and when data would be replaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedures must be adhered to exactly in subsequent experiments or the Stage 2 manuscript can be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: procedural detail and replicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe experimental procedures in sufficient detail to allow another researcher to repeat the methodology exactly without requiring further information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures must be adhered to exactly at Stage 2 or risk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis pipeline specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a proposed analysis pipeline, including all preprocessing steps and precise description of all planned analyses, including appropriate correction for multiple comparisons. Any covariates or regressors must be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where analysis decisions are contingent on prior analyses, specify those contingencies and adhere to them. Only pre-planned analyses can be reported in the main Results section of Stage 2; unplanned exploratory analyses are admissible in a separate section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical power analysis requirement (Neyman–Pearson inference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies involving Neyman–Pearson inference must include a statistical power analysis. Estimated effect sizes should be justified with reference to existing literature and power analysis must be based on the lowest available or meaningful estimate of effect size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases of highly uncertain effect sizes, variable sample size and interim data analysis is permissible but requires pre-specified inspection points, appropriate Type I error correction for ‘peeking’, and a final stopping rule. Proposed a priori power levels should be justified for all hypothesis tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bayesian methods guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: For Bayesian hypothesis testing, predictions of the theory must be specified so a Bayes factor can be calculated; indicate what distribution will represent the predictions and how parameters will be specified (e.g., uniform, normal/half-normal, JZS/Cauchy with specified scaling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should aim for a Bayes factor strength likely to be useful to readers and, if stopping depends on Bayes factor, indicate a maximum feasible sample size after which sampling will stop. Prospective authors are encouraged to read key references (e.g., Schönbrodt & Wagenmakers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome-neutral quality checks specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide full descriptions of any outcome-neutral criteria that must be met for successful testing of stated hypotheses (e.g., absence of floor or ceiling effects, positive controls, or other quality checks orthogonal to hypotheses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These checks are used at Stage 2 to determine whether the data are able to test the hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and resubmission date at Stage 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a timeline for completion of the study and a proposed resubmission date if Stage 1 review is successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions can be negotiated with the editorial office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tense and wording conventions for Stage 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Any description of prospective methods or analysis plans should be written in future tense in Stage 1 submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At Stage 2 these should be converted to past tense where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot data policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot data are optional but can be included to establish proof of concept, effect size estimates, or feasibility of methods. Any pilot experiments will be published with the final manuscript and clearly distinguished from main data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary registrations / secondary analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal welcomes submissions proposing secondary analyses of existing datasets, provided authors can supply sufficient evidence (e.g., self-certification; letter from independent gatekeeper) to confirm they had no prior access to the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses are not considered for the Registered Report format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 reviewer assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers at Stage 1 will assess: originality and validity of research question(s); extent to which proposed study can satisfactorily answer the question(s); logic, rationale, and plausibility of hypotheses; soundness and feasibility of methodology and analysis pipeline (including power analysis); clarity and degree of methodological detail sufficient to exactly replicate procedures and analysis; whether authors pre-specified sufficient outcome-neutral tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following Stage 1 review manuscripts will be rejected, offered revision, or accepted in principle (AIP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance in principle (AIP) conditions and protocol registration
rubrics_metrics.description: AIP indicates the article will be published pending completion of approved methods and analytic procedures, passing all pre-specified quality checks, and a defensible interpretation of results. Stage 1 protocols are not published following AIP; authors must register the protocol in a recognized repository (publicly or under embargo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific Reports offers to host Stage 1 protocols on figshare and keep under embargo until Stage 2 acceptance; if authors deposit independently, the registration must be public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviation handling after AIP
rubrics_metrics.description: Any deviation from stated experimental procedures, regardless of perceived minor status, could lead to rejection at Stage 2. If the protocol is altered due to unforeseen circumstances, authors must consult editors immediately and prior to completion of data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor changes may be permitted at editorial discretion and reported in Stage 2; substantial changes require withdrawal and resubmission as a new Stage 1. Registered analyses must be undertaken; additional unregistered analyses can be included as exploratory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 cover letter requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 2 cover letter must confirm that the manuscript includes a link to the public archive containing anonymized study data, digital materials/code and the laboratory log; that the manuscript contains a link to the approved Stage 1 protocol in a standalone 'Protocol Registration' section; and that, for primary Registered Reports, no data for any pre-registered study (other than Stage 1 pilot data) was collected prior to the date of AIP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For secondary Registered Reports, authors should confirm that no data (other than Stage 1 pilot data) were subjected to the pre-registered analyses prior to AIP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data, materials and code availability at Stage 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymized raw data, digital experimental materials, and code must be made freely available in a public repository that provides a DOI to ensure persistence, uniqueness, and citability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data files should be time-stamped to show data were collected after AIP; raw data must be accompanied by guidance notes to help replication; upload analysis scripts and other materials that assist replication. Raw data should be archived in a repository rather than submitted as journal supplementary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory log requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must provide a basic laboratory log outlining the range of dates during which data collection took place, uploaded to the same public archive as data and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 immutability of Introduction and hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Apart from minor stylistic revisions, the Introduction cannot be altered from the approved Stage 1 submission, and the stated hypotheses cannot be amended or appended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any textual changes must be clearly marked in the Stage 2 submission. New literature appearing after AIP should be covered in the Discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of registered analyses and handling flawed registered analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The outcome of all registered analyses must be reported in the Stage 2 manuscript; exceptions apply only if a registered and approved analysis is subsequently shown to be logically flawed or unfounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an analysis is shown flawed, the authors, reviewers, and editor must agree it is inappropriate; the analysis would still be mentioned in Methods but omitted with justification from Results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploratory (unregistered) analyses policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional analyses not included in the registered submission are admissible but must be clearly justified, appropriately caveated, and reported in a separate Results section titled 'Exploratory analyses'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be careful not to base conclusions entirely on statistically significant post hoc analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical reporting requirements (NHST)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors reporting null hypothesis significance tests are required to report exact p values, effect sizes and confidence intervals for all inferential analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 reviewer assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers at Stage 2 will assess whether: the data are able to test the proposed hypotheses by satisfying approved outcome-neutral conditions; the Introduction, rationale and hypotheses are the same as Stage 1; the authors adhered precisely to registered experimental procedures; any unregistered post hoc analyses are justified and methodologically sound; and whether the authors' conclusions are justified given the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may suggest additional post hoc tests, but authors are not obliged to perform them unless necessary to satisfy Stage 2 review criteria. Editorial decisions will not be based on perceived importance, novelty, or conclusiveness of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript withdrawal and Withdrawn Registration policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors with AIP may withdraw their manuscript; the journal will publicly record each case by publishing a Withdrawn Registration article containing authors, proposed title, the abstract from the approved Stage 1 submission, and brief reasons for failure to complete the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial withdrawals are not possible; incomplete studies by the Stage 2 deadline (unless extended by negotiation) will be considered withdrawn and subject to a Withdrawn Registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incremental registrations (adding experiments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may add experiments to approved submissions; the approved Stage 2 manuscript will be accepted for publication and authors can propose additional experiments for Stage 1 consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where experiments extend the approved submission, editorial team will seek to fast-track review. If an incremented submission is rejected, authors retain the option to publish the most recently approved version of the manuscript.
